hook: A helium fluorescence lidar measures upper-atmosphere temperature at 500 to 700 km altitude
summary: Temperatures above about 500 km are hard to measure from the ground. A lidar in Danzhou, China, detects faint fluorescence from metastable helium using a three-wavelength laser and single-photon detectors. Profiles broadly track radar ion temperatures, but the comparison is only qualitative since the instruments measure different quantities.
title: Temperature Measurements up to 700 km Using Metastable Helium Fluorescence LiDAR
